crop.notes: Most of the clipping is the unrelated 'Jockey Dugan in the Ascendency on Local Tracks' racing column (headline cut on the right). Only the last part, below a rule ('about 170 pounds. Few of the great English fighters...' to '...equal in other respects.'), mentions Allen. From the page layout this fragment appears to be a jump of the adjacent interview 'John L. Sullivan Says He Wants to Become a Farmer' (the speaker says 'no kind of argument could ever convince me'), not part of the jockey story. The rest of that interview is not in the clipping.

ocr.notes: Jockey text mostly readable; the Allen passage has key errors ('16-pounder' and '2-pounder' for 165-pounder and 200-pounder, '= Mitchell' for Charlie Mitchell). Headline garbled.

title.suggested: John L. Sullivan Recalls Tom Allen's Fighting Weight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch printed remarks, apparently by John L. Sullivan, that Tom Allen fought at 165 pounds and always held that a well-conditioned 165-pounder could beat a 200-pounder under London prize ring rules.

metadata.notes: Masthead: Sunday Morning, St. Louis Post-Dispatch, September 18, 1904, page 7B (sports page). Attribution of the passage to Sullivan is inferred from the page layout and should be checked on the full-resolution page.

facts.fact: Allen always maintained that a thoroughly conditioned 165-pounder could beat a 200-pounder under London prize ring rules (reported secondhand, apparently by John L. Sullivan, who disagreed)

notes: Recrop needed: drop the jockey column and clip the Allen passage together with the John L. Sullivan interview it seems to belong to; confirm the speaker on the full page.
